label: Which role owns this task?
prompt: Click the role that typically owns each responsibility. Some tasks could involve multiple roles — pick the primary owner.

items.task: Style the checkout button so it stands out on mobile screens
items.explanation: Visual styling and responsive behavior is frontend work — implementing the designer's spec in CSS/JS.

items.task: Write the SQL query that calculates monthly revenue by region
items.explanation: Database queries and business logic live on the server. The backend exposes results via an API endpoint.

items.task: Set up automated deployments whenever code merges to the main branch
items.explanation: CI/CD pipelines, deployment automation, and infrastructure-as-code are core DevOps responsibilities.

items.task: Create wireframes and a user flow for the new onboarding screens
items.explanation: Wireframes, user flows, and overall UX structure are the designer's primary output before implementation begins.

items.task: Add rate limiting so the public API can't be abused
items.explanation: API security, rate limiting, and server-side validation are backend concerns — they must happen server-side to be enforceable.

items.task: Monitor server CPU and alert on-call when it spikes above 90%
items.explanation: Observability, alerting, and on-call infrastructure are owned by DevOps (or a platform/SRE team at larger companies).
